question: Is the proposed combined recipe (same-passage context-graph supervision + adaptive one-hop repair + RL on lower-hop items with deeper-hop transfer evaluation) already fully published, leaving no novel contribution?
description: The first literature probe returned arxiv:2609.12230, 'Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering' (2026), whose abstract describes every component of the idea: attaching supporting triples from the same source text chunk to each primary KG triple to form a context graph, two supervision settings (KG-grounded vs CG-grounded), adaptive LLM-judged repair of unresolved one-hop failures, RL on lower-hop QA items, and evaluation on 3-hop/4-hop/5-hop tasks with Qwen3-14B. The project directory name also contains 'scooped', consistent with this. If confirmed, the idea is a replication and the contribution must be re-scoped (e.g., to an independent ablation of which component drives the gain, or to generalization beyond disease-specific KGs).
confidence_basis: Verified full-text quotes from the paper's own contribution list and method sections, corroborated by its abstract, unambiguously describe all four components; residual uncertainty is only about unpublished implementation details.
rationale: Determines whether any contribution remains; must be resolved before investing in experiments. One retrieved paper already appears to cover the full mechanism, but only the abstract has been read and no full text is available yet, so the extent of overlap (exact ablations, datasets, baselines, metrics) is unverified.
resolution: Resolved by reading the full text: arxiv:2609.12230 does implement the complete combined recipe. Its contribution bullets and Section 3.3 state the same-source-chunk context-triple attachment and the KG-grounded vs CG-grounded supervision comparison, Section 3.6 describes the LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair of unresolved one-hop failures with quarantine, and the abstract/contributions describe lower-hop RL with 3-5-hop evaluation on Qwen3-14B. Method overlap is 1.0 and no novel mechanism remains in the idea as stated; only evaluation protocol and scope distinguish it.
